title.narrative: Addressing sexual and reproductive health and protection needs and risks of eastern flood-affected women, adolescent girls including pregnant women and person with disabilities

description.narrative: UNFPA, through an integrated SRH-GBV intervention, aims to respond effectively to the life-saving Protection and Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) needs of approximately 21,907 women, adolescents, and transgender people. This intervention responds to some of the most critical needs of the vulnerable groups as a result of the flood, which can have life-changing impacts (e.g. child marriage, maternal mortality, mental health).Deployment of 30 midwives in selected union-level health facilities to provide life-saving maternal health services and gradually more comprehensive sexual and reproductive (SRH) services. Mentoring of project and government midwives and other maternity ward staff by 03 clinical doctors at the union and upazila level health facilities to ensure quality services and referral follow-up. Ensure essential logistics and supplies in 15 union-level health facilities to facilitate quality services.Refresher orientation of midwives, doctors, family welfare visitors (FWV) and health managers on MISP, SRH, and PSS/PFA services.Orientation of volunteers (community, youth, FWV, etc.) on SRH services, psychological first aid (PFA), gender-based violence (GBV) core concepts, crisis counseling, and safe referral. Community mobilization by volunteers, youth volunteers, and youth-led organizations to sensitize communities on SRH and GBV services for women and adolescent girls.40 mobile SRH camps at the union level providing lifesaving reproductive health care services, MHPSS, and GBV referrals, particularly to women and girls. Cash for SRH and referral to 300 pregnant women for institutional delivery and management of obstetric complications. Distribution of 1,860 baby kits among flood-affected pregnant women seeking services at the union and upazila level facilities. Support existing SRH coordination at the district level in the affected areas, including coordination with GBV cluster / WG on addressing health response gaps. Distribution of 3,000 Menstrual health management (MHM) kits among adolescent girls (10- 19 years) including girls with disabilities in the affected communities, including those seeking services in the SRH mobile camp.. Life-saving information will be disseminated to adolescents and young people regarding adolescent sexual and reproductive health (ASRHR), sexually transmitted diseases (STIs), and safe management of reproductive health. Distribute cash for dignity kits to 2,500 flood-affected pregnant and lactating women coming to the health facilities for services and delivery. Deployment of 6 roving MHPSS counselors/ GBV case workers in health facilities to ensure counseling, GBV case management, and safe referrals.
